children: Lundbeck's study results for epilepsy drug candidate bexicaserin could soon prove the Danish drugmaker's multiyear efforts to turn around its research-and-development operations are bearing fruit, analysts at UBS say in a note. The study results could underscore the drug's potential to become a blockbuster product and be the first datapoint of Lundbeck's shift away from its legacy in psychiatry to areas with more predictable trial outcomes, the analysts say. "R&D  turnaround is one of the hardest challenges in the pharma industry. Only a few companies have successfully done it, and we think Lundbeck could be one of them," they add. UBS raises its recommendation on Lundbeck's stock to buy from neutral, and lifts its target price to 52 Danish kroner from 45 kroner. Shares rise 2.9% to 43.80 kroner. (adria.calatayud@wsj.com)
